SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1, PDF p.8

4.3.1 Presentation of the document

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.1, PDF p.8

4.3.1.1 This document defines the modes of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment (see chapter 4.4 “Definition of the modes” and chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.2, PDF p.8

4.3.1.2 This document gives all transitions between modes (see chapter 4.6 “Transitions between modes”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.3, PDF p.8

4.3.1.3 This document describes the possible exchanged information between the driver and the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, respect to the mode (see chapter 4.7 “DMI depending on modes”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.4, PDF p.8

4.3.1.4 This document describes how the received information is filtered, respect to several criteria such as the level, the mode, etc.. (see chapter 4.8 “Acceptance of received information”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.5, PDF p.8

4.3.1.5 This document describes how the stored information is handled, respect to several criteria such as the level, the mode, etc. (see chapter 4.9 “What happens to accepted and stored information when entering a given level”, and chapter 4.10 “What happens to accepted and stored information when entering a given mode”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.6, PDF p.8

4.3.1.6 All the tables that are included in this document shall be considered as mandatory requirements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.1.7, PDF p.8

4.3.1.7 Some notes appear in this document. These notes are here to help the reader to understand the specifications, or to explain the reason(s) of a requirement.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.2, PDF p.8

4.3.2 Identification of the possible modes

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.3.2.1, PDF p.8

4.3.2.1 List of the modes: Full Supervision (FS) Limited Supervision (LS) On Sight (OS) Staff Responsible (SR) Shunting (SH) Unfitted (UN) Passive Shunting (PS) Sleeping (SL) Stand By (SB) Trip (TR)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.8

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP Post Trip (PT) System Failure (SF) Isolation (IS) No Power (NP) Non Leading (NL) National System (SN) Reversing (RV)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.9

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4, PDF p.10

4.4 Definition of the modes

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.1.1, PDF p.10

4.4.1.1 For each mode the following information is given: a) The context of utilisation of the mode and the functions that characterise the mode (chapter “Description”). b) The ERTMS/ETCS levels in which the mode can be used (chapter “Used in levels”). c) The related responsibility of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment and of the driver, once the equipment is in this mode (chapter “Responsibilities”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.1.2, PDF p.10

4.4.1.2 A complete list of transitions to and from each mode is given in the section 4.6.2 “Transitions Table” ).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.2, PDF p.10

4.4.2 General Requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.2.1, PDF p.10

4.4.2.1 When the desk is open, a clear indication of the ERTMS/ETCS mode shall be shown to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.2.2, PDF p.10

4.4.2.2 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.10

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.1.1, PDF p.11

4.4.3.1.1 In Isolation mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall be physically isolated from the brakes and can be isolated from other on-board equipments/systems depending on the specific on-board implementation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.1.2, PDF p.11

4.4.3.1.2 There shall be a clear indication to the driver that the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is isolated.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.1.3, PDF p.11

4.4.3.1.3 To leave Isolation mode, a special operating procedure is needed (no transition from Isolation is specified). This procedure shall ensure that the on-board equipment is only put back into service when it has been proven that this is safe for operation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.1.4, PDF p.11

4.4.3.1.4 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.2.1, PDF p.11

4.4.3.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.3.1, PDF p.11

4.4.3.3.1 Isolation of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is performed by the driver under his complete responsibility.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.3.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.3.3.2, PDF p.11

4.4.3.3.2 Once the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is isolated, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has no more responsibility.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.11

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.1.1, PDF p.12

4.4.4.1.1 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is not powered, the equipment is in the No Power mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.1.1.1, PDF p.12

4.4.4.1.1.1 Note: in order to ensure cold movement detection function, some parts of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment may be fed by an auxiliary power supply.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.1.2, PDF p.12

4.4.4.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall permanently command the emergency brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.1.3, PDF p.12

4.4.4.1.3 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.2.1, PDF p.12

4.4.4.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.3.1, PDF p.12

4.4.4.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has no responsibility in this mode, except commanding the emergency brake and (optionally) monitoring cold movements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.3.2, PDF p.12

4.4.4.3.2 The notion of responsibility of the driver is not relevant for the No Power mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.4.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.4.3.3, PDF p.12

4.4.4.3.3 If it is required to move a loco in NP mode as a wagon, ETCS brake command must be overridden by external means.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.12

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.1.1, PDF p.13

4.4.5.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to the System Failure mode in case of a fault, which affects safety.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.1.2, PDF p.13

4.4.5.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall permanently command the Emergency Brakes.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.1.3, PDF p.13

4.4.5.1.3 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.2.1, PDF p.13

4.4.5.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.3.1, PDF p.13

4.4.5.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for commanding the Emergency Brakes.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.5.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.5.3.2, PDF p.13

4.4.5.3.2 No responsibility of the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.13

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.1, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.1 The Sleeping mode is defined to manage the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of a slave engine that is remote controlled.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.2, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.2 The desk(s) of a sleeping engine must be closed (since there is no driver, no information shall be shown).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.3, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.3 As the engine is remote controlled by the leading engine, its ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall not perform any train movement supervision.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.4, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the Train Position function; in particular, the front/rear end of the engine (i.e., not the train) shall be used to refer to train front/rear end.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.5, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.5 Sleeping mode shall be automatically detected on-board via the train interface.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.6, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.6 If possible, the train must not be stopped due to a safety critical fault in a sleeping engine. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment should therefore try to memorise the occurrence of such fault(s), which should be handled when the engine leaves the Sleeping mode. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment should also try to send an error information to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.7, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.7 If a desk of the sleeping engine is opened while the train is running (this is an abnormal operation), the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to Stand-By mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.8, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.8 If the “sleeping input signal” is lost (no more detection of the remote control), the switch to Stand-By mode shall be made only if the train is at standstill.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.9, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.9 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.10, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.10 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall open a communication session with the RBC when at least one of the following events occurs: a) in all levels, on receipt of the order to contact the RBC. b) In level 2/3, when entering or exiting Sleeping mode (to report the change of mode to the RBC). c) In level 2/3, when a safety critical fault of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment occurs (to report the fault to the RBC).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.11, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.11 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.12

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.12, PDF p.14

4.4.6.1.12 In case of balise group message consistency error (refer to 3.16.2.4.4 and 3.16.2.5.1), the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall not command the service brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.14

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.1.13

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.1.13, PDF p.15

4.4.6.1.13 When in levels 2 or 3, if no compatible version has been established between the on- board equipment in Sleeping mode and the RBC, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall react as specified in 3.5.3.7 d) 2nd bullet but no driver’s indication shall be given.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.2.1, PDF p.15

4.4.6.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.3.1, PDF p.15

4.4.6.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of an engine in Sleeping mode has no responsibility for the train protection.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.3.2, PDF p.15

4.4.6.3.2 The notion of responsibility of the driver is not relevant for the Sleeping mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.6.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.6.3.2.1, PDF p.15

4.4.6.3.2.1 Note: The leading engine is responsible for the movement of the train. It is then the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of the leading engine that is fully/partially/not responsible for the train protection, with respect to its mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.15

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.7.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.1, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.1 The Stand-By mode is a default mode and cannot be selected by the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.7.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.2, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.2 It is in the Stand-By mode that the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment awakes.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.7.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.3, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.3 Data for mission are collected in Stand-By (see SRS-chapter 5: “Start of Mission” procedure).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.7.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.4, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.4 In Stand-By mode, the desk of the engine can be open or closed. No interaction with the driver shall be possible as long as the desk is closed, except isolation of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.7.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.5, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the Standstill Supervision.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.1.6, PDF p.16

4.4.7.1.6 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.2.1, PDF p.16

4.4.7.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.3.1, PDF p.16

4.4.7.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for maintaining the train at standstill.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.7.3.2, PDF p.16

4.4.7.3.2 The driver has no responsibility for train movements.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.16

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.1, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.1 The purpose of the Shunting mode is to enable shunting movements. In Shunting mode, The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise the train movements against: a) a ceiling speed: the shunting mode speed limit b) a list of expected balise groups (if such list was sent by the trackside equipment). The train shall be tripped if a balise group, not contained in the list, is passed (When an empty list is sent, no balise group can be passed. When no list is sent, all balise groups can be passed) c) “stop if in shunting mode” information. The train is tripped if such information is received from balise groups d) Intentionally deleted

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.2, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.2 The Shunting mode shall not require Train Data.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.3, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the Train Position function

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.4, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.4 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.5, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.5 When in Shunting mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall not manage level transitions. However, an immediate level transition order or a conditional level transition order shall be stored and evaluated only when another mode than Shunting or Passive Shunting has been entered (i.e. when the Shunting movement is terminated).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.5.1, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.5.1 When receiving a communication session establishment order, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board in Shunting mode shall not establish the communication session, but shall store the RBC ID/phone number.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.5.2, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.5.2 When in Shunting mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall not manage RBC-RBC hand-over, except for storing the RBC ID/phone number given at the RBC/RBC border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.6, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.6 Shunting mode can be selected by the driver, only accepted when the train is at standstill, or ordered by the trackside.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.7, PDF p.17

4.4.8.1.7 In case of selection of Shunting mode by the driver:  in level 1 operations, the switch to shunting is always accepted by the on-board equipment  in level 2 and 3 areas, the on-board asks the trackside for an authorisation. The switch to shunting is possible only after receiving such authorisation. The trackside can send a list of balises, that the train is allowed to pass while in SH, together with the authorisation

4.4.8.1.8 In case of order to switch to Shunting mode from trackside, the order:  in level 1 is given by a balise group. A list of balises, that the train is allowed to pass after the entry in Shunting, can be sent together with the order  in level 2 and 3 is sent via radio. A list of balises, that the train is allowed to pass after the entry in Shunting, can be sent together with the order

4.4.8.1.9 When the switch to shunting is ordered by trackside, a driver acknowledgement is requested.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.9.1, PDF p.18

4.4.8.1.9.1 Note: in Shunting mode the train is only partially supervised, therefore it is necessary that the driver takes the responsibility.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.10, PDF p.18

4.4.8.1.10 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed and, only on driver request, the permitted speed. The display of the permitted speed shall also be stopped on driver request.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.1.11, PDF p.18

4.4.8.1.11 Intentionally deleted.

4.4.8.1.12 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.2.1, PDF p.18

4.4.8.2.1 Used in level 0, NTC, 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.3.1, PDF p.18

4.4.8.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for the supervision of the shunting mode speed limit, and that the engine with the active antenna is tripped when passing the defined border of the shunting area (only if there is a defined border: balise group not in the list given by trackside, or balise group giving the information “stop if in shunting”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.8.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.8.3.2, PDF p.18

4.4.8.3.2 The driver is responsible for: a) Remaining inside the shunting area defined by a procedure or an external system outside ERTMS/ETCS (also when the shunting area is protected by balises) b) Train/engine movements and shunting operations

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.18

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.1, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall be in the Full Supervision mode when all train and track data, which is required for a complete supervision of the train, is available on board.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.2, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.2 Full supervision cannot be selected by the driver, but is entered automatically when all necessary conditions are fulfilled.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.3, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.3 To be in Full Supervision mode, SSP and gradient are not required for the whole length of the train, but must be available at least from the FRONT END of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.4, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.4 Once in Full Supervision mode, if SSP and gradient are not known for the whole length of the train, an indication “ENTRY IN FULL SUPERVISION” shall be clearly displayed to the driver until SSP and gradient are known for the whole length of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.4.1, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.4.1 Note: this indication may also be displayed in case the train length has been increased, see 3.18.3.8.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.5, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against a dynamic speed profile.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.6, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed, the permitted speed, the target distance and the target speed to the driver (this list is not exhaustive – refer to chapter 4.7 “DMI depending on modes”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.1.7, PDF p.19

4.4.9.1.7 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.2.1, PDF p.19

4.4.9.2.1 Used in level 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.3.1, PDF p.19

4.4.9.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is fully responsible for the train protection (except for the 2 situations described below).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.3.2, PDF p.19

4.4.9.3.2 The driver is responsible for respecting the EOA when approaching an EOA with a release speed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.9.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.9.3.3, PDF p.19

4.4.9.3.3 When “ENTRY IN FULL SUPERVISION” is displayed to the driver, the driver is responsible for respecting speed restrictions that apply for the part of the train that is not covered by SSP and gradient data.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.19

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.1, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.1 The Unfitted mode is used to allow train movements in either: a) Areas that are equipped neither with ERTMS/ETCS track-side equipment nor with national train control system b) Intentionally deleted c) Areas that are equipped with ERTMS/ETCS trackside equipment and/or national train control system(s), but operation under their supervision is currently not possible

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.2, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against a ceiling speed: the lowest of the maximum train speed and the Unfitted mode speed limit for unfitted area (national value).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.2.1, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.2.1 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.3, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall also supervise temporary speed restrictions.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.4, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.1.5, PDF p.20

4.4.10.1.5 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.2.1, PDF p.20

4.4.10.2.1 Used in level 0.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.3, PDF p.20

4.4.10.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.3.1, PDF p.20

4.4.10.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment supervises a ceiling speed and (if available) temporary speed restrictions.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.10.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.10.3.2, PDF p.20

4.4.10.3.2 The driver must respect the existing line-side signals and is fully responsible for train movements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.20

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.1, PDF p.21

4.4.11.1.1 The Staff Responsible mode allows the driver to move the train under his own responsibility in an ERTMS/ETCS equipped area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.2, PDF p.21

4.4.11.1.2 This mode is used when the system does not know the route. For example: a) After the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment starts-up (awakening of the train). b) To pass a signal at danger / override an EOA. c) After a trackside failure (for example: loss of radio contact).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.3, PDF p.21

4.4.11.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against: a) a ceiling speed: the staff responsible mode speed limit b) a given distance (regarding its origin location see 4.4.11.1.3.1). The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise braking curves with a target speed of zero to the end of this distance. If the train overpasses this distance (see next note) the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall trip the train c) a list of expected balise groups, if this list has been sent by the RBC. The train shall be tripped if over-passing a balise group that is not in the list. (When an empty list is sent, no balise group can be passed. When no list is sent, all balise groups can be passed) d) balise groups giving the order ‘stop if in SR’. This order shall immediately trip the train, unless the over-passed balise group is included in a list of expected balises as defined in item c) e) running in the direction opposite to the train orientation (reverse movement protection)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.3.1, PDF p.21

4.4.11.1.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall determine the start location of the SR distance as follows: a) If the National/Default value determines the max permitted distance to run in SR mode, the starting point of this distance shall refer to the estimated position of the train front when SR mode was entered, or, already in Staff Responsible mode, when Override was activated. b) If the max permitted distance to run in SR mode is determined by the value transmitted by the RBC, or entered by the driver, the start location of the distance shall refer to the estimated position of the train front when the distance information is received or entered. c) If the max permitted distance to run in SR mode is determined by the value transmitted by EUROLOOP, the distance information transmitted by EUROLOOP shall be referred to one or more reference balise groups. On-board shall evaluate

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.21

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP the distance to run in SR mode by matching the reference balise groups given with the LRBG. In case the LRBG is, due to a change of orientation, in front of the train when the distance to run in SR mode is to be determined from the EUROLOOP information, the complete distance to run in SR mode shall be determined as the distance given by EUROLOOP plus the distance between the estimated train front end and the LRBG.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.4, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.4 Note: Since the gradient is unknown, the supervision of the braking curves in Staff Responsible mode does not ensure that the train will not pass the given distance.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.5, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall give the possibility to the driver to modify the value of the SR mode speed limit and of the given distance. This shall be possible only at standstill.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.5.1, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.5.1 If a train movement is detected while the driver is entering the SR speed/distance limits, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall trigger the brake command.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.5.2, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.5.2 The unit, range and resolution of the SR mode speed limit and distance entered by the driver shall be as specified in A.3.11.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6 If the level is 2/3 and a communication session is open, the driver shall have the possibility to request a new distance to run in Staff Responsible, by selecting "Start". This triggers an MA request.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.1, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.1 Note: Once the SR distance is covered, the driver may have to go further.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.2, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.2 When entering SR mode, the value applicable for SR mode speed limit and the value applicable for SR distance shall be the corresponding National/Default values. Exception for SR distance: SR mode is authorised by RBC giving an SR distance.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.3, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.3 While in SR mode, the value applicable for the SR mode speed limit shall be, if available, the last value entered by the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.4, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.4 While in SR mode, the value applicable for the SR distance shall be, if available, the last value received by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment amongst: a) the distance to run in SR entered by the driver; b) the distance to run in SR given by trackside.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.5, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.5 When "Override" is selected, the SR mode speed limit value and the SR distance value previously entered by driver or given by trackside, if any, shall be deleted. The corresponding National/Default values shall enter in force.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.6, PDF p.22

4.4.11.1.6.6 If the train is in SR and receives a new distance to run in SR mode from the RBC, the stored list of expected balise groups, if any, shall be deleted or shall be replaced by the list of expected balise groups sent together with the distance to run in SR.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.22

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.6.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.6.7, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.6.7 If an ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment in SR mode, after having received from EUROLOOP max permitted distance to run in SR mode information, detects the main signal balise group being part of this information then it shall ignore any new max permitted distance to run in SR mode information from that loop.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.7, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.7 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed and the (when active) override (permission to pass a signal at danger, trip inhibited). The permitted speed, target distance and the target speed shall be displayed only on driver request, until the driver requests to stop their display.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.8, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.8 Intentionally deleted.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.9, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.9 If receiving a "track ahead free" request from the RBC, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment requests the driver to enter the "track ahead free" information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.10, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.10 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.1.11, PDF p.23

4.4.11.1.11 Intentionally deleted.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.2.1, PDF p.23

4.4.11.2.1 Level 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.3, PDF p.23

4.4.11.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.3.1, PDF p.23

4.4.11.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment supervises a ceiling speed, a SR distance if finite and, if available, a list of balises.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.3.2, PDF p.23

4.4.11.3.2 The driver must check if the track is free, if points are correctly positioned, and must respect the existing line-side information (signals, speed boards etc.).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.11.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.11.3.3, PDF p.23

4.4.11.3.3 When using the possibility to modify the value of the SR mode speed limit and of the given distance, the driver is responsible for entering reasonable values.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.23

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.1, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.1 The On Sight mode enables the train to enter into a track section that could be already occupied by another train, or obstructed by any kind of obstacle.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.2, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.2 On Sight mode cannot be selected by the driver, but shall be entered automatically when commanded by trackside and all necessary conditions are fulfilled.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.3, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against a dynamic speed profile.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.4, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed to the driver. The permitted speed, target distance, target speed and release speed (if any) shall be displayed only on driver request, until the driver requests to stop their display (this list is not exhaustive – refer to chapter 4.7 “DMI depending on modes”).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.5, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.5 If receiving a "track ahead free" request from the RBC, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment requests the driver to enter the "track ahead free" information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.6, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.6 To be in On Sight mode, SSP and gradient are not required for the whole length of the train, but must be available at least from the FRONT END of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.7, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.7 Once in On Sight mode, if SSP and gradient are not known for the whole length of the train, an indication “ENTRY IN ON SIGHT” shall be clearly displayed to the driver until SSP and gradient are known for the whole length of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.7.1, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.7.1 Note: this indication may also be displayed in case the train length has been increased, see 3.18.3.8.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.1.9, PDF p.24

4.4.12.1.9 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.2.1, PDF p.24

4.4.12.2.1 Used in level 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.3, PDF p.24

4.4.12.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.3.1, PDF p.24

4.4.12.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for the supervision of the train movements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.12.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.12.3.2, PDF p.24

4.4.12.3.2 The driver is responsible for checking the track occupancy when moving the train, because the track may be occupied.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.24

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.1.1, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.1.1 Note: Application of emergency brakes and train trip are two different things. For example, exceeding the permitted speed leads to application of the emergency brakes, but as long as the train does not pass the EOA/LOA, it is not a train trip.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.2, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall command the emergency brakes (no brake release is possible in Trip mode).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.3, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall indicate to the driver the reason of the train trip.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.4, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request an acknowledgement from the driver once train is at standstill (to allow the driver to acknowledge the train trip).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.4.1, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.4.1 Note: This acknowledgement is mandatory to exit from Trip mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.5, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.5 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.1.6, PDF p.25

4.4.13.1.6 Closing the desk while being in Trip mode will not cause a mode change but no interaction with the driver shall be possible as long as the desk is closed, except isolation of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.2.1, PDF p.25

4.4.13.2.1 Used in level 0, NTC, 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.3, PDF p.25

4.4.13.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.3.1, PDF p.25

4.4.13.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for stopping the train and for maintaining the train at standstill.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.13.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.13.3.2, PDF p.25

4.4.13.3.2 The driver has no responsibility for train movements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.25

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.1, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.1 The Post Trip mode shall be entered immediately after the driver acknowledges the trip.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.2, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.2 Once in post trip mode, the onboard equipment shall release the Command of the emergency brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.2.1, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.2.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall keep on indicating to the driver the reason of the train trip.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.3, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.3 The train shall only be authorised to move backwards a given distance (national value). The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise this national distance for reverse movements, and shall command the service brakes if the distance is over- passed. The driver shall be informed about the reason for the brake application.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.3.1, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.3.1 Note: The ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment performs the Reverse Movement Protection (as in PT mode, the "normally allowed movement" is backwards, then the Reverse Movement Protection avoids the train running in forward direction when in PT mode). This implies that the given distance to run backwards in PT is considered as a directional data, oriented backwards.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.3.2, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.3.2 After the release of a brake command initiated due to an overpassed distance allowed for moving backwards in Post Trip mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall command the service brake for any further movement in the direction opposite to the train orientation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.4, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.4 When moving backwards in Post Trip mode, the train trip shall be inhibited.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.5, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.5 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.6, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.6 When ERTMS/ETCS level is 1, if the driver selects “Start” the onboard equipment proposes Staff Responsible. When ERTMS/ETCS level is 2 or 3, the selection of Start leads to an MA Request to the RBC. It is the RBC responsibility to give an SR authorisation, or a Full Supervision MA or an On Sight/Shunting MA to an ERTMS/ETCS equipment that is in Post Trip mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.7, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.7 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.8, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.8 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.1.9, PDF p.26

4.4.14.1.9 In case of balise group message consistency error (refer to 3.16.2.4.4 and 3.16.2.5.1), the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall not command the service brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.26

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.2.1, PDF p.27

4.4.14.2.1 Used in level 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.3, PDF p.27

4.4.14.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.3.1, PDF p.27

4.4.14.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for supervising that the train moves only backwards and that the backward movement does not exceed the maximum permitted distance (national value).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.14.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.14.3.2, PDF p.27

4.4.14.3.2 The driver is responsible if moving the train backwards.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.27

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.1, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.1 The Non-Leading mode is defined to manage the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of a slave engine that is NOT electrically coupled to the leading engine (and so, not remote controlled) but has its own driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.1.1, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.1.1 Note: This operating situation is called Tandem.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.1.2, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall use, as a necessary condition to enter in Non-Leading mode, a “non leading input signal" from the train interface.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.1.3, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.1.3 If the “non leading input signal" is no longer present, the switch to Stand-By mode shall be made only if the train is at standstill.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.2, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall not perform any train movement supervision in Non-Leading mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.3, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the Train Position function; in particular, the front/rear end of the engine (i.e., not the train) shall be used to refer to train front/rear end.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.4, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.4 When level is 2 or 3, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall report its position to the RBC, according to the previously received parameters.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.5, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.5 If possible, the train must not be stopped due to a safety critical fault in a non-leading engine. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment should therefore try to memorise the occurrence of such fault(s), which should be handled when the engine leaves Non Leading mode. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment should also try to send an error information to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.6, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.7, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.7 Intentionally deleted

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.8, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.8 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.9, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.9 The supervision of linking consistency shall not be performed in Non Leading mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.1.10, PDF p.28

4.4.15.1.10 In case of balise group message consistency error (refer to 3.16.2.4.4 and 3.16.2.5.1), the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall not command the service brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.2.1, PDF p.28

4.4.15.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.28

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.3, PDF p.29

4.4.15.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.3.1, PDF p.29

4.4.15.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment performs NO protection functions, except forwarding track conditions associated orders through DMI or train interface.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.15.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.15.3.2, PDF p.29

4.4.15.3.2 The driver is responsible for obeying the orders associated to track conditions, when they are displayed by the DMI.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.29

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.16

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.16, PDF p.30

4.4.16 Intentionally deleted

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.30

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17, PDF p.31

4.4.17 National System (SN) mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.1.1, PDF p.31

4.4.17.1.1 In SN mode, according to the specific on-board implementation, the National System may access the following resources via the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment: DMI, Juridical Recording interface, odometer, train interface and brakes. This can be achieved through the STM interface.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.1.2, PDF p.31

4.4.17.1.2 A limited set of data coming from balises shall be used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, refer to SRS chapter 4.8 “Use of received information”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.1.3, PDF p.31

4.4.17.1.3 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.3, PDF p.31

4.4.17.3 Responsibilities of ERTMS/ETCS Onboard

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.3.1, PDF p.31

4.4.17.3.1 No train supervision functionality is provided by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment. In case the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is interfaced to the National System through an STM, refer to the FFFIS STM (Subset 035) for the functionality provided by ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.3.2, PDF p.31

4.4.17.3.2 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.4, PDF p.31

4.4.17.4 Responsibilities of the National System

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.4.1, PDF p.31

4.4.17.4.1 The National System is responsible for all train supervision and protection functions.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.4.2, PDF p.31

4.4.17.4.2 The National System is responsible for issuing and revoking brake command.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.4.3, PDF p.31

4.4.17.4.3 The National System is responsible for maintaining national system behaviour and interact with national trackside equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.4.4, PDF p.31

4.4.17.4.4 The National System is responsible for interaction with the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.5, PDF p.31

4.4.17.5 Responsibilities of the driver

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.17.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.17.5.1, PDF p.31

4.4.17.5.1 The responsibility of the driver depends on the National System in use.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.31

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.1, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.1 The Reversing mode allows the driver to change the direction of movement of the train and drive from the same cab, i.e. the train orientation remains unchanged. This is possible only in areas so marked by trackside.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.2, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.2 Note: This mode is used to allow the train to escape from a dangerous situation and to reach as fast as possible a “safer” location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.3, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against: a) a ceiling speed: the Reversing mode speed limit given from trackside b) a distance to run in the direction opposite to the train orientation, given from trackside. The emergency brake shall be commanded if overpassing this distance

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.4, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.4 After the release of a brake command initiated due to an overpassed reversing distance, and while the reversing distance is still overpassed, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment shall command the emergency brake for any further movement in the direction opposite to the train orientation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.5, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed, the permitted speed and the remaining distance to run.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.6, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.6 In case the SBI supervision limit is exceeded (refer to chapter 3 table 5, triggering condition t4), the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall command the emergency brake instead of the service brake. For the revocation of the brake command, refer to 3.13.10.2.4.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.7, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.7 The position reports sent when in reversing mode shall refer to the location of the driving cab (as before reversing).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.8, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.8 Note: The ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment performs the Reverse Movement Protection (as in RV mode, the "normally allowed movement" is backwards, then the Reverse Movement Protection avoids the train running in forward direction when in RV mode). This implies that the given distance to run in reversing is considered as a directional data, oriented backwards.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.9, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.9 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.10, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.10 In case of balise group message consistency error (refer to 3.16.2.4.4 and 3.16.2.5.1), the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall not command the service brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.11, PDF p.32

4.4.18.1.11 In case there is an alarm reporting a malfunction for the onboard balise transmission function, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall ignore this alarm.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.32

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.1.12

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.1.12, PDF p.33

4.4.18.1.12 In case the ERTMS/ETCS system version number X transmitted by any balise is greater than the highest version X supported by the onboard equipment (refer to 3.17.3.5), the information from this balise shall be ignored, the train shall not be tripped and the driver shall not be informed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.2.1, PDF p.33

4.4.18.2.1 Level 1, 2, 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.3, PDF p.33

4.4.18.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.3.1, PDF p.33

4.4.18.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment supervises a ceiling speed and a distance to run in reverse direction.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.18.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.18.3.2, PDF p.33

4.4.18.3.2 The driver must keep the train movement inside the received distance to run.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.33

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19, PDF p.34

4.4.19 LIMITED SUPERVISION

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.1, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.1 The Limited Supervision mode enables the train to be operated in areas where trackside information can be supplied to realise background supervision of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.2, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.2 Limited supervision can not be selected by the driver, but shall be entered automatically when commanded by trackside and all necessary conditions are fulfilled.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.3, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall supervise train movements against a dynamic speed profile.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the train speed and the release speed, if any (this list is not exhaustive – refer to chapter 4.7 “DMI depending on modes”). Upon request by trackside (refer to clauses 4.4.19.1.4.2 to 4.4.19.1.4.6) if the generic LS function marker is stored on-board or if the conditions in clause

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.7, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.7 are fulfilled, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall also display the lowest speed amongst: a) the lowest MRSP element between the minimum safe front end of the train and the EOA/LOA, AND b) the target speed at the EOA/LOA

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.1, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.1 The speed resulting from 4.4.19.1.4 a) and b) is called the Lowest Supervised Speed within the Movement Authority (LSSMA)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.2, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.2 Upon an order to toggle on the LSSMA display, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall start a delay timer: a) For order received from RBC/RIU: at the value of the time stamp of the message including the order. b) For order received from balise group: at the time of passage over the first encountered balise of the balise group giving the order. c) Exception to a) and b): for order that has been stored in the level transition buffer (see section 4.8.3): at the time the level transition is performed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.3, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.3 When the delay timer value becomes greater than the time-out value given by trackside, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the LSSMA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.4, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.4 On reception of an order to toggle (on or off) the LSSMA display, a toggle on order which has not been executed yet (because the on-board delay timer has not reached the delay time-out value) shall be deleted by the on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.5, PDF p.34

4.4.19.1.4.5 If the LSSMA display is already toggled on, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall toggle off the LSSMA display in case:

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.34

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP a) the clause 4.4.19.1.4.3 is not immediately fulfilled upon reception of a new order to toggle on the LSSMA display b) an order to toggle off the LSSMA display is received.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.6, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.4.6 When entering the Limited Supervision mode, the LSSMA display shall be toggled off by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, unless a toggle on order is received and leads immediately to the display of the LSSMA as per clauses

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.2, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.4.2 and 4.4.19.1.4.3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.7, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.4.7 If the generic LS function marker is not stored on-board, the clauses 4.4.19.1.4.2 to 4.4.19.1.4.6 shall not apply and the LSSMA shall be displayed if: a) the target speed at the EOA/LOA is lower than the Limited Supervision mode speed limit, AND b) the LSSMA is lower than the maximum train speed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.4.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.4.8, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.4.8 The generic LS function marker shall be deleted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment as soon as a Limited Supervision mode profile is received without it in the same balise group message.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.5, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.5 If receiving a "track ahead free" request from the RBC, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment requests the driver to enter the "track ahead free" information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.6, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.6 To be in Limited Supervision mode, SSP and gradient are not required for the whole length of the train, but shall be at least available from the FRONT END of the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.1.7, PDF p.35

4.4.19.1.7 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to 4.5 “Modes and on- board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.2.1, PDF p.35

4.4.19.2.1 Used in levels 1, 2 and 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.3, PDF p.35

4.4.19.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.3.1, PDF p.35

4.4.19.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for the background supervision of the train movement to the extent permitted by the information provided by trackside.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.3.1.1, PDF p.35

4.4.19.3.1.1 Note: The Limited Supervision mode enables the train to be operated in areas equipped with lineside signals where ETCS does not have information regarding the status of some signals, i.e. not all signals are fitted with LEUs or connected to an RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.3.2, PDF p.35

4.4.19.3.2 The driver must always observe the existing line-side information (signals, speed boards etc.) and National operating rules.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.19.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.19.3.2.1, PDF p.35

4.4.19.3.2.1 Note: the indications given to the driver by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment do not substitute the observance of the line-side information. In particular the display of the LSSMA, if deemed necessary by the trackside, only complements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.35

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP the line-side information, e.g. in case there could be a discrepancy between this latter and the background supervision.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.36

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.1, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.1 The Passive Shunting mode is defined to manage the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of a slave engine (NOT remote controlled, but mechanically coupled to the leading engine), being part of a shunting consist. This mode can also be used to carry on a shunting movement with a single engine fitted with one on-board equipment and two cabs, when the driver has to change the driving cab.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.2, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.2 The desk of a Passive Shunting engine must be closed (since there is no driver, no information shall be shown).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.3, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.3 As the engine is coupled to a leading engine, its ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall not perform any train movement supervision.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.4, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform Train Position function; in particular, the front/rear end of the engine (i.e., not the train) shall be used to refer to train front/rear end.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.5, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.5 It shall only be possible to enter in Passive Shunting mode from the Shunting mode; while in Shunting mode, the driver shall have the possibility to enable the function “Continue Shunting on desk closure”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.6, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.6 When the active desk is closed, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to Passive Shunting mode if the function “Continue Shunting on desk closure” is active and the “passive shunting input signal” is received from the train interface. If the function “Continue Shunting on desk closure” is not active or the “passive shunting input signal” is not present, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to Stand-By mode instead.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.7, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.7 The special function “Continue Shunting on desk closure” shall allow one and only one transition from Shunting mode to Passive Shunting mode. The special function shall be inactive once the Shunting mode is left.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.8, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.8 If a desk of the Passive Shunting engine is opened and no “Stop Shunting on desk opening” information previously received from balise group is stored onboard, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.9, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.9 If a desk of the Passive Shunting engine is opened and “Stop Shunting on desk opening” information previously received from balise group is stored onboard, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch to Stand By mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.10, PDF p.37

4.4.20.1.10 If possible, the train must not be stopped due to a safety critical fault in a Passive Shunting engine. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment should therefore try to memorise the occurrence of such fault(s), which should be handled when the engine leaves the Passive Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.37

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.11, PDF p.38

4.4.20.1.11 When in Passive Shunting mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall not manage level transitions. However, an immediate level transition order or a conditional level transition order shall be stored and shall be evaluated only when another mode than Shunting or Passive Shunting has been entered (i.e. when the Shunting movement is terminated).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.12

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.12, PDF p.38

4.4.20.1.12 When receiving a communication session establishment order, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board in Passive Shunting mode shall not establish the communication session, but shall store the RBC ID/phone number information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.13

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.13, PDF p.38

4.4.20.1.13 When in Passive Shunting mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall not manage RBC- RBC hand-over, except for storing the RBC ID/phone number information given at the RBC/RBC border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.14

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.14, PDF p.38

4.4.20.1.14 Note: for the list of main functions related to this mode, refer to chapter 4.5 “Modes and on-board functions”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.1.15

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.1.15, PDF p.38

4.4.20.1.15 In case of balise group message consistency error (refer to 3.16.2.4.4 and 3.16.2.5.1), the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall not command the service brake.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.2.1, PDF p.38

4.4.20.2.1 Used in all levels: Level 0, level 1, level 2, level 3 and level NTC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.3, PDF p.38

4.4.20.3 Responsibilities

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.3.1, PDF p.38

4.4.20.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of an engine in Passive Shunting mode has no responsibility for the train protection.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.3.2, PDF p.38

4.4.20.3.2 The notion of responsibility of the driver is not relevant for the Passive Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.4.20.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.4.20.3.3, PDF p.38

4.4.20.3.3 Note: The leading engine is responsible for the movement of the train. It is then the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of the leading engine that is fully/partially/not responsible for the train protection, with respect to its mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.38

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

4.6 Transitions between modes

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.1, PDF p.44

4.6.1.1 The indication “4>” means: The condition n°4 must be fulfilled to trigger the transition

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.2, PDF p.44

4.6.1.2 From the mode located in the column

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.3, PDF p.44

4.6.1.3 To the mode that is indicated by the arrow “>”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.4, PDF p.44

4.6.1.4 Each transition from a given mode receives a priority order (indicated by “-px-”, x is the priority order) to avoid a conflict between the different transitions when they occur at the same time (i.e. in the same clock cycle). P1 has a higher priority than P2.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.5, PDF p.44

4.6.1.5 Some transitions have received the same priority order. This has been decided when it is obvious that these transitions cannot occur at the same time, and so can never lead to a conflicting situation (for example, the RBC cannot give in the same time a MA for FS and a MA for OS to a given engine, this is why the transition “from SR to FS” and the transition “from SR to OS” have the same priority order).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.6.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.6.1.6, PDF p.44

4.6.1.6 "16, 17, 18" means "16 or 17 or 18".

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7, PDF p.50

4.7 DMI depending on modes

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.1.1, PDF p.50

4.7.1.1 The DMI is an interface that allows the direct exchange of information between the driver and the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment. The indirect exchange of information done via the train interface (e.g. a driver’s action on the service brake used for the service brake feedback, opening/closing the desk) is not part of the DMI.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.1.2, PDF p.50

4.7.1.2 The device(s) used to select “ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment powered/unpowered” is (are) not part of the DMI.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.1.3, PDF p.50

4.7.1.3 The device(s) used to select/indicate “ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment isolated/not isolated” is (are) part of the DMI.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.1.4, PDF p.50

4.7.1.4 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.1.5, PDF p.50

4.7.1.5 Information (input or output) only relevant for National System and not originated by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board is not included in the following section.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.2, PDF p.50

4.7.2 DMI versus Mode Table

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.2.1.1, PDF p.50

4.7.2.1.1 X = active: For a DMI output, this means that the output information shall be shown to the driver when the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment is in the mode indicated in the column. For a DMI input, this means that it shall be possible for the driver to enter this information when the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment is in the mode indicated in the column).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.7.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.7.2.1.2, PDF p.50

4.7.2.1.2 A = available: This means that the input/output shall become active ONLY if another condition(s) is (are) fulfilled. This condition(s) are not described here.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8, PDF p.55

4.8 Acceptance of received information

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.1, PDF p.55

4.8.1.1 The aim of this chapter is to give an overview of which information is accepted or rejected depending on the state of the on-board (level, mode) and the nature of the received information (transmission medium, type of information: infill or non-infill).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.2, PDF p.55

4.8.1.2 The following sections have to be interpreted by applying the filters as shown in Figure 3. The first filter is detailed in section 4.8.3 “Accepted information depending on the level and transmission media”, the third filter in section 4.8.4 “Accepted information depending on the modes”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.3, PDF p.55

4.8.1.3 If a message contains level transition information, any other information in that message shall be evaluated considering the level transition information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.3.1, PDF p.55

4.8.1.3.1 Information received in the same message as an immediate level transition order or a conditional level transition order that causes a level transition shall be evaluated first considering the on-board currently operated level, as if a level transition order for further location had been received (i.e. conditions [1], [2] or [6] of Figure 3, if applied, shall be automatically fulfilled). Then, if relevant, it shall be immediately extracted from the buffer and re-evaluated according to the new selected level.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.4, PDF p.55

4.8.1.4 Note: As shown in Figure 3, information stored following an announcement of a change of level, is re-checked for acceptance when the level has changed. This implies that, when the level changes, the mode is - for a short moment – still unchanged, until the stored information has been processed. The consequence for the Third Filter is that information needs to be accepted for this short period also in modes in which this information is otherwise useless.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.5, PDF p.55

4.8.1.5 If a message contains infill information, this latter shall be evaluated considering all other non-infill information in that message.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.1.6, PDF p.55

4.8.1.6 When evaluating trackside information received by radio or when re-evaluating a set of information released from the transition buffer, linking information, if any, shall be evaluated prior to any other location related information.
