SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.2.1, PDF p.57

4.8.2.1 The following tables shall be applied assuming that: a) the information complies with the system version checks (see section 3.17.3) and with the data consistency checks.(see section 3.16) b) the direction for which the information is valid matches the current train orientation, or the balise group crossing direction (for SL, PS and SH engines).(see section 3.6.3) c) In levels 2/3, it is assumed that the “RBC” information which is marked “A” (Accepted) comes from the supervising RBC (see RBC/RBC handover). If this information is received from the “Accepting” RBC while the “Handing Over” RBC is still responsible, it is stored onboard until the RBC transition is performed Exception 1: The information “Acknowledgement of Train Data”, “Trackside constituent system version”, "Session Management" and “Acknowledgement of Session Termination" shall be immediately accepted. Exception 2: The information “Co-operative shortening of MA”, “Revocation of Emergency Stop” and “LSSMA display toggle on/off order” shall be rejected. d) to check exception [4] in 4.8.3, the track description is referred to the LRBG (i.e. relocation has been performed see 3.6.4.3). e) the information from balise is received while no reverse movement is performed (see clause 3.14.3.6)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.2.2, PDF p.57

4.8.2.2 Regarding 4.8.2.1 a): In case a balise is missed or a balise telegram cannot be decoded, the information “Inhibition of balise group message consistency reaction” is only used by the on-board equipment to inhibit the service brake reaction, while the balise group message is rejected. If all the telegrams from a balise group are correctly read, the information “Inhibition of balise group message consistency reaction”, if received, shall be ignored by the on-board equipment. Therefore this information need not to be referred to in the following tables.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.2.3, PDF p.57

4.8.2.3 In case a balise telegram contains the information VBC marker and a country/region identity that both match a stored VBC, the whole balise telegram is ignored and any further check in relation to this balise telegram is irrelevant (refer to 3.15.9.3 b)). Otherwise the information VBC marker, if included in a consistent balise group message, shall always be ignored by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment and need not to be referred to in the following tables.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.2.4, PDF p.57

4.8.2.4 Note: with the exception of the data that is forwarded to a National System through the STM interface (see 3.15.6 and SUBSET-035), what will happen to the data to be used by applications outside ERTMS/ETCS (e.g. whether it is discarded, forwarded to an external application, processed by a national function…) is outside the scope of this specification and is assumed as not being part of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board functionality.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5, PDF p.68

4.8.5 Handling of transition buffer in case of level transition announcement or RBC/RBC handover

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.1, PDF p.68

4.8.5.1 If an order to switch to level NTC, 1, 2 or 3 at a further location has been received, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall be able to store in a transition buffer (see figure 3, first filter) three sets of information obtained from three filtered messages.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.2, PDF p.68

4.8.5.2 If a RBC transition order has been received and the Handing Over RBC is still the supervising one, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall be able to store in a transition buffer (see figure 3, second filter) three sets of information obtained from three filtered messages from the Accepting RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.2.1, PDF p.68

4.8.5.2.1 Note: the term “set of information” refers to the part of a message being stored in the transition buffer (i.e. information which is neither accepted nor rejected immediately) according to the conditions stated in 4.8.3.1 [1] and [2] (for level transition) or according to 4.8.2.1c (for RBC/RBC handover).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.3, PDF p.68

4.8.5.3 In case three sets of information are already stored in the transition buffer, any new set to be stored shall replace the oldest one currently stored.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.4, PDF p.68

4.8.5.4 The sets of information stored in the transition buffer shall be deleted: a) in case the level transition order is deleted or overwritten by another level transition order for a different level, OR b) in case the RBC transition order is deleted or overwritten by an order to switch to another Accepting RBC, OR c) in case the communication session with the RBC that provided the stored information is terminated

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.5, PDF p.68

4.8.5.5 At the same time the level transition is performed or at the same time the Accepting RBC becomes the supervising one, the sets of information stored in the transition buffer shall be released and re-evaluated in the sequence they have been received.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.6, PDF p.68

4.8.5.6 This sequential re-evaluation of all the released information shall be a prerequisite to any use by the on-board equipment (e.g. it will lead neither to an intermediate change of mode nor to a change of information displayed to the driver) and shall obey the following principles: a) Starting from the information currently used by on-board at the moment the level/RBC transition is effective, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall determine the new information for train supervision, by performing sequential updates from the information released from the transition buffer, if accepted. b) For each information update related to a re-evaluated set of information, the same rules shall apply as to information update related to new information accepted outside a level/RBC transition context.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.68

3.6.0 Chapter 4: Modes and Transitions 13/05/2016 ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP c) The information resulting from this sequential update shall then be used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.7, PDF p.69

4.8.5.7 Accepting re-evaluated Conditional Emergency Stop information according to table

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.3, PDF p.69

4.8.3 implies that the accepted Conditional Emergency Stop information may be accepted or rejected in a further step (see clause 3.10.2.2) depending on the given stop location. This decision, based on the comparison between the min safe front end position of the train at the time the message was received and the given stop location, shall be considered part of the evaluation process as it affects the further re-evaluation of information stored in the transition buffer (see clause 3.10.2.4).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.7.1, PDF p.69

4.8.5.7.1 Note: For the case of the Unconditional Emergency Stop information accepting the information according to table 4.8.3 will always lead to the train being tripped (see clause 3.10.2.3) when re-evaluation of the transition buffer is completed. Information accepted during re-evaluation of information stored in the transition buffer can then be affected on transition to TR mode according to conditions in Table 4.10.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.8.5.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.8.5.8, PDF p.69

4.8.5.8 Note: The requirement to acknowledge an Emergency Stop information according to clause 3.10.1.4, i.e., communicating to the RBC if the information has been accepted (Conditional or Unconditional Emergency Stop) or rejected because the train has passed the stop location (Conditional Emergency Stop only), applies to the time when the information is used, immediately after the sequential update has been completed. Regards acknowledging the reception of an emergency stop message, as for any other information received from trackside, see clause 3.16.3.5.

4.9 What happens to accepted and stored information when entering a given level

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.9.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.9.1.1, PDF p.70

4.9.1.1 Every data that can be stored onboard after being accepted may be influenced by a level transition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.9.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.9.1.2, PDF p.70

4.9.1.2 A level transition acts on the “status” of stored information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.9.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.9.1.3, PDF p.70

4.9.1.3 In case of entering level 1, MA Request Parameters, Position Report Parameters and Track Ahead Free Request shall be deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.9.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.9.1.3.1, PDF p.70

4.9.1.3.1 In case of entering level 0, NTC or 1, the information “Inhibition of revocable TSRs from balises in L2/3” shall be deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.9.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.9.1.4, PDF p.70

4.9.1.4 For all other stored data, a level transition has no effect (void).

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.11.1.1, PDF p.75

4.11.1.1 Status of stored information, which is set to "Invalid" when No Power mode is entered, shall be affected, when relevant, by information from the Cold Movement Detection function, according to the following table: Status of On-board stored information EOLM Train Position ERTMS/ETCS Table of trackside RBC ID/Phone information Level supported levels Number Transition conditions Un- Invalid Vali Un- Invalid Valid Un- Invalid Valid Un- Invalid Valid Un- Invalid Valid known d known know known known n No Cold movement      occurred Cold movement detected or   Cold movement information not available

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.11.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.11.1.2, PDF p.75

4.11.1.2 Note: Status of stored information, which remains valid after NP mode has been entered, is not affected by information from the Cold Movement Detection function.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 4.11.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 4.11.1.3, PDF p.75

4.11.1.3 If a cold movement has been detected, or the Cold Movement Detection function is not able to confirm that no cold movement has taken place, no change of status of information to “valid” shall be made until it has been validated by a different means than cold movement detection.

1.0.0 Updated after comments from Unisig meeting 17-02-00 in N. Lindström 21-02-00 Stuttgart:  New concept for redundancy (send all telegrams on both busses if redundant bus is attached);  New concept for retransmission (send all telegrams twice on each bus);  New command numbers for nonfail-safe telegrams;  Transition table added;  Added an informal appendix describing provided services;  Editorial updates.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 1.0.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 1.0.1, PDF p.2

1.0.1 Updated after comments from Alstom and Siemens N. Lindström 23-02-00  Removed authentication for nonfail-safe connections  Corrected command number for nonfail-safe telegrams in paragraph 5.1.1.5.  Added paragraph 5.6.1.1  Added paragraph 8.1.1.1.  Editorial improvements.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 1.0.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 1.0.2, PDF p.2

1.0.2 Updated after comments from Unisig meeting 22-03-00 in N. Lindström 28-03-00 Paris and CENELEC meeting 09-03-00:  Added section for definitions and improved several definitions.  Updated the document to the new redundancy concept  Removed the non-safe communication in favour for low safe communication.  Removed the CRC-32 for safe communication. The CRC is to be defined.  Added a CRC-16 for low safe communication.  Added message format for multicast telegrams. Implicit data is sent explicit for multicast telegrams (measure for hazard: incorrect ID).  Added the functionality that a connection can be disconnected by “application” and reconnected thereafter.  Improved disconnect_reason in the Disconnect Telegram.  Idle_cycle_interval is sent in the Connect Request and Connect Confirm telegrams.  Added Dual_bus in the Connect Request and Connect Confirm telegrams, make it possible to monitor if the connection is using one or two busses.  Clarified Isolation (Failure mode) and disconnection of a connection.  Editorial improvements.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.1, PDF p.10

3.3.1.1 A node is a physical device that communicates through STM busses. A node has one physical bus address but may have several logical addresses (Service Access Point, SAP).

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.1.1, PDF p.10

3.3.1.1.1 A node can contain several logical functions defined in /3/ (e.g. the same node will be able to gather logical functions Odometer, Juridical Data).

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.2, PDF p.10

3.3.1.2 Intentionally deleted SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 10/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.3, PDF p.11

3.3.1.3 To ensure correct operation of the communication between two nodes, a connection is established:

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.3.1, PDF p.11

3.3.1.3.1 A point-to-point connection is used for the communication between two nodes.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.3.2, PDF p.11

3.3.1.3.2 A multicast message is a message simultaneously sent to all nodes.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.4, PDF p.11

3.3.1.4 A point-to-point connection may have different safety levels:

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.4.1, PDF p.11

3.3.1.4.1 A point-to-point connection with Safety Level 0 (SL 0) is a connection between two nodes whereof one node is non-safe (SIL 0).

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.4.2, PDF p.11

3.3.1.4.2 A point-to-point connection with Safety Level 2 (SL 2) is a connection which shall be used by nodes with at least SIL 1.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.4.3, PDF p.11

3.3.1.4.3 A point-to-point connection with Safety Level 4 (SL 4) is a connection which shall be used by nodes with at least SIL 3.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.4.4, PDF p.11

3.3.1.4.4 A SIL 4 equipment shall be able to handle point-to-point connections with any Safety Level and a SIL 2 equipment shall be able to handle point-to-point connections with SL 2 and SL 0.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.5, PDF p.11

3.3.1.5 A station is the part of a device relating to the processing of one bus. The term station is defined in /2/.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.6, PDF p.11

3.3.1.6 The communication between two nodes is done via one or two busses. The node may be equipped with one or two stations.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.7, PDF p.11

3.3.1.7 Logical connection master is defined as the node sending the connection request telegram for a point-to-point connection in the Safe Link Layer.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.8, PDF p.11

3.3.1.8 Logical connection Master is the master of a logical connection. A logical connection has one and only one master.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.9, PDF p.11

3.3.1.9 Logical connection slave of point-to-point connection is defined as the node sending the Connect Confirm telegram in the Safe Link Layer.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.10, PDF p.11

3.3.1.10 Logical connection Slave is the slave of a logical connection. A point-to-point logical connection has one and only one Logical connection Slave.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.11, PDF p.11

3.3.1.11 A Multicast connection has one Multicast Sender.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.3.1.12

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.3.1.12, PDF p.11

3.3.1.12 A Multicast connection may have zero, one or several Multicast Receivers.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.1, PDF p.11

3.4.1.1 PROFIBUS is an open field bus to which any PROFIBUS-compatible equipment can be attached. To satisfy the requirements of a single-channel safety-related transmission system, it is necessary to use an additional safety layer. The protocol for SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 11/62 3.1.0 data transmission with error detection specified in this document enables the relevant requirements of the CENELEC standard /1/ to be met.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.1.1, PDF p.12

3.4.1.1.1 Note: The requirements of the CENELEC standard are not achieved by the Safe Link Layer alone. Only the complete set of specifications  STM FFFIS (SUBSET-035),  STM FFFIS Safe Time Layer (SUBSET-056) and  STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer (SUBSET-057) together fulfil all the listed requirements.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.2, PDF p.12

3.4.1.2 The protocol for data transmission with error detection provides a method of error detection for individual telegrams. The telegram error detection system uses unique sender/receiver identification, a 32-bit sequence number and a CRC error detection suffix.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.3, PDF p.12

3.4.1.3 A requirement for the protocol for data transmission with error detection is to set up connections between nodes and monitor these connections cyclically.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.4, PDF p.12

3.4.1.4 For increased availability, a redundant configuration of PROFIBUS can be implemented (physical diversity). All telegrams are sent on both busses.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.5, PDF p.12

3.4.1.5 For increased availability, the following provisions are provided:

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.5.1, PDF p.12

3.4.1.5.1 Multicast telegrams are sent twice from the Safe Link Layer to the lower layer.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.5.2, PDF p.12

3.4.1.5.2 Point-to-point telegrams are sent once from the Safe Link Layer to the lower layer but with the PROFIBUS FDL ACK / NACK protocol with one retransmission.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.6, PDF p.12

3.4.1.6 To establish an SL 4 or an SL 2 point-to-point connection, two steps have to be performed: 1. connection set-up with the exchange of random numbers. 2. authentication, to ensure the safety property of the communication partners

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.7, PDF p.12

3.4.1.7 To establish an SL 0 connection only the connection set-up has to be performed.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.8, PDF p.12

3.4.1.8 The Safe Link Layer provides communication with three levels of safety (SL): 1. Safety Level 4 (SL 4) 2. Safety Level 2 (SL 2) 3. Safety Level 0 (SL 0)

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.8.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.8.1, PDF p.12

3.4.1.8.1 Justification: According to the CENELEC standard /1/ the command numbers, sequence numbers, SAP and CRC have to be different for connections with different safety levels. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 12/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.4.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.4.1.9, PDF p.13

3.4.1.9 All nodes that are physically connected to the bus have the safety requirement that they shall not implement any SL protocol corresponding to a higher Safety Integrity Level (SIL) than their own SIL. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 13/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.5

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.5, PDF p.14

3.5 Scope of this Document

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.5.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.5.1.1, PDF p.14

3.5.1.1 This document describes the protocol for data transmission with error detection and the PROFIBUS FDL services used to transfer the data to the PROFIBUS FDL driver. The mode of transfer and variant of the PROFIBUS interface used depend on the implementation and are not specified in this document. The PROFIBUS itself and PROFIBUS protocol are specified in /2/. PROFIBUS FDL parameters are out of the scope of this specification, but defined in /3/.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.5.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.5.1.2, PDF p.14

3.5.1.2 Note: the time stamp functionality shown in the diagram on application level uses the STL layer Reference Time service. Signalling hazard Time stamp for signalling / Application Application domain application Time stamp for safe bus Bus communication Safe Time Layer Safe Time Layer communication hazard domain Scope of this Sequence number, identity Safe Link Layer Safe Link Layer specification and CRC Redundancy Unsafe redundancy Redundancy supervisor supervisor Unsafe bus FDL FDL Unsafe bus FDL FDL Figure 1 Scope of the protocol specification

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 3.5.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.5.1.3, PDF p.14

3.5.1.3 The redundancy supervisor is a non-safe function that is only required if the node is equipped with dual busses. The redundancy supervisor is specified in section 9.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 3.5.1.4, PDF p.14

3.5.1.4 Dual busses is not mandatory. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 14/62 3.1.0 4. PROFIBUS INTERFACE (FDL)

4.1.1.1 The protocol defined here is designed for PROFIBUS FDL masters for multicast and point-to-point communication.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 4.1.1.2, PDF p.15

4.1.1.2 All the point-to-point telegrams for data transmission are transferred using the same PROFIBUS FDL service.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 4.1.1.3, PDF p.15

4.1.1.3 Point-to-point telegrams shall be transferred by means of send_data_with_acknowledge (SDA) with one retransmission.

5.1 General Structure of a Telegram

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.1.1.1, PDF p.16

5.1.1.1 The telegrams shall have the following fixed telegram frame: 5.1.1.2 Telegram header Telegram trailer for data transmission for data transmission with error detection with error detection PROFIBUS Net data PROFIBUS header trailer Command CRC Lowest-order byte of sequence number (least significant data, LSD) Scope of this protocol description The black fields are the PROFIBUS FDL header and trailer. Figure 2 General structure of a point-to-point telegram

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.1.1.3, PDF p.16

5.1.1.3 Note: The PROFIBUS FDL header and trailer are part of the PROFIBUS FDL protocol and can be found in the CENELEC standard /2/. A detailed description of the elements of the PROFIBUS FDL protocol is not given here. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 16/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.1.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.1.1.4, PDF p.17

5.1.1.4 Detailed protocol structure of the telegram: 5.1.1.5 Byte Designation Range of values Meaning 1 Lowest_order_byte_ 0..FFh Of the 32-bit sequence number only the 8 lowest-order bits are sequence_number transmitted here. The 24 higher-order bits are used for CRC formation only (implicit data). 2 Command 80h.BFh Command for SL 4 data transmission with error detection: 80h: connect request telegram 81h: not used and reserved 82h: connect confirm telegram 83h: authentication telegram 84h: authentication acknowledgement telegram 85h: disconnect telegram 86h: idle telegram 87h: not used and reserved (send disable telegram) 88h: not used and reserved (send enable telegram) 89h: telegram for upper layer 8Ah: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover telegram) 8Bh: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover acknowledgement) 8Ch: not used and reserved 8Dh: multicast telegram for upper layer 8Eh..9Fh: reserved for future extension of the Safe Link Layer A0h..BFh: telegram for upper layer 00h..3Fh Command for SL 2 data transmission with error detection: 00h: connect request telegram 01h: not used and reserved 02h: connect confirm telegram 03h: authentication telegram 04h: authentication acknowledgement telegram 05h: disconnect telegram 06h: idle telegram 07h: not used and reserved (send disable telegram) 08h: not used and reserved (send enable telegram) 09h: telegram for upper layer 0Ah: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover telegram) 0Bh: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover acknowledgement) 0Ch: not used and reserved 0Dh: not used and reserved 0Eh..1Fh: reserved for future extension of the Safe Link Layer 20h..3Fh: telegram for upper layer SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 17/62 3.1.0 Byte Designation Range of values Meaning C0h..FFh Command for SL 0 data transmission with error detection: C0h: connect request telegram C1h: not used and reserved C2h: connect confirm telegram C3h: not used and reserved (authentication telegram) C4h: not used and reserved (authentication acknowledgement telegram) C5h: disconnect telegram C6h: idle telegram C7h: not used and reserved (send disable telegram) C8h: not used and reserved (send enable telegram) C9h: telegram for upper layer CAh: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover telegram) CBh: not used and reserved (redundancy switchover acknowledgement) CCh: not used and reserved CDh: not used and reserved CEh..DFh: reserved for future extension of the Safe Link Layer E0h..FFh: telegram for upper layer 3.. Net_data In the data telegram the application data is transferred here. In internal (n-l) telegrams, e.g. connect request telegrams, the structure of the net data is command-specific (see sections below). n =< 244 bytes (max. length of “DATA_UNIT”, see /2/); for 'l' see below (n-l+1) CRC as per safety level l: length of CRC checksum:.. n

5.1.3.4 Structure of the implicit data: Byte Designation Range of values Meaning 1 Data_length 2..244 The length of the user data bytes (“DATA_UNIT” from the PROFIBUS FDL viewpoint) in the telegram, i.e. length of telegram header for data transmission with error detection + length of net data + length of telegram trailer for data transmission with error detection 2 Receiver_address 0..126 The receiver's address can be handled as implicit data because it is available on the PROFIBUS FDL. 3 Sender_address 0..126 The sender's address can be handled as implicit data because it is available on the PROFIBUS FDL. 4 DSAP 0..62 The partner's service access point can be handled as implicit data because it is available on the PROFIBUS FDL. 5 SSAP 0..62 The local service access point can be handled as implicit data because it is available on the PROFIBUS FDL. 6..8 Higher_order_24bits 000000h.. Except for the lowest-order byte, the sequence number does not _of_sequence_numb FFFFFFh need to be transmitted. The receiver adds the known higher- er order bits of the sequence number to the lowest-order byte transferred.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.1.4.1, PDF p.20

5.1.4.1 An authentication shall be performed to start an SL 4 or an SL 2 connection. The authentication is used to check that the connection has the required Safety Level (SL). This implies that computers/units of at least the required Safety Integrity Level (SIL) are being used at either end of the connection for data transmission. Random numbers modified by an algorithm known only to computers with the respective Safety Integrity Level are exchanged in separate telegrams (see 5.2.3 and 5.2.4).

The 24 higher-order bits are used for CRC formation only. The sequence number of this telegram is the same as the random number field below. 2 Command 80h or 00h or C0h Command for data transmission with error detection: Connect Request telegram 3..6 Random_number 00000000h.. A random number representing the sequence number for the FFFFFFFFh telegram is created randomly and transmitted. 7..8 Idle_cycle_timeout 0..65500 Max. time between the reception of two telegrams that the receiver of this message has to check according to chapter 5.2.6 in ms: 0: no supervision of the idle_cycle_timeout 100..65500: idle_cycle_timeout in steps of 100 ms. 9 Configuration data 0..255 Value = 3 prefix X 10 Configuration data 0..255 Value = 0 prefix Y 11 Configuration data 0..255 Value = 0 prefix Z 12 Dual bus 0..255 0: The node is not equipped with dual busses 1: The node is equipped with dual busses 2..255: not used (reserved) 13.. net_data Data from upper layers n-l n <= 244 bytes (max. length of “DATA_UNIT”, see /2/) l: length of CRC checksum n-l+1.. CRC As per Safety CRC as per Safety Level n Level

If the Authentication telegram does not arrive in time, or the authentication is faulty, a Disconnect telegram is issued (final disconnection). SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 22/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.2.3, PDF p.23

5.2.3 Authentication Telegram

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.2.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.2.3.1, PDF p.23

5.2.3.1 Introduction: Besides the connection establishment proper, successful connection set- up of SL 4 and SL 2 connections also requires authentication. The authentication is used to check that the connection has the required Safety Level (SL). This implies that the two nodes wishing to establish the connection are at least of the required Safety Integrity Level (SIL). To detect this, a random number is used as the initial sequence number in the Connect Request telegram as specified above. Secondly, the random number in the authentication received with the Connect Confirm telegram is processed using the algorithm specified in section 5.1.4. The processed random number (= authentication number) is exchanged with the Authentication telegram/Authentication Acknowledgement and checked at the receiving end.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.2.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.2.3.2, PDF p.23

5.2.3.2 Authentication is used to improve the distinction between communication of different safety levels.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 5.2.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.2.3.3, PDF p.23

5.2.3.3 The Authentication Telegram shall not be transmitted in case of an SL 0 connection.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.2.3.4, PDF p.23

5.2.3.4 Structure of the Authentication telegram, transmitted data: Byte Designation Range of values Meaning 1 Lowest_order_byte_ 0..255 Of the 32-bit sequence number only the 8 lowest-order bits are sequence_number transferred. The 24 higher-order bits are used for CRC formation only. This sequence number is incremented by one with respect to the Connect Request telegram. 2 Command 83h or 03h Command for data transmission with error detection: Authentication telegram 3..6 Authentication_num 00000000h.. The authentication number is the received random number after ber FFFFFFFFh processing by the defined algorithm (see chapter 5.1.4). 7.. CRC CRC as per Safety Level 7+l l: length of CRC checksum

If the Authentication Acknowledgement fails to arrive in time, or the Authentication Acknowledgement is faulty, a Disconnect telegram shall be issued (final disconnection). SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 23/62 3.1.0

5.3.1.1 Before data can be transferred between two nodes, a connection must be established. The connection set-up shall be performed in two steps:  connection set-up  authentication

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 5.3.1.3, PDF p.30

For this purpose, the received random numbers in each partner shall be modified using a defined algorithm (see section 5.1.4) and exchanged via the Authentication telegrams.

5.5.1.3.1 Incorrect telegram received; as laid out in the specification there is a single and a double fault possible. A double fault occurs if a corrupted telegram occurs two times within a defined period (see chapter 5.2.5.8.4) in a connection with higher Safety Level. For Safety Level 0 connections, all incorrect receives are considered first incorrect receive. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 38/62 3.1.0

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.1.1.6, PDF p.43

6.1.1.6 Since multicast is a 1-to-N transmission there is no possible data flow from receiver to sender on any level. As a consequence the receiver does not acknowledge any Multicast Data Telegram.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 6.1.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.1.1.7, PDF p.43

6.1.1.7 Multicast messages are allowed to be lost occasionally. The following message will provide an update, and the lost message is no longer needed. One consecutive multicast being lost or corrupted should be acceptable as a minimum. This shall be handled by the upper layer.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 6.1.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.1.1.8, PDF p.43

6.1.1.8 If the bus is realised redundantly all multicast messages shall be sent on both redundant busses. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 43/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 6.1.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.1.1.9, PDF p.44

6.1.1.9 As the sender is expected to transmit all Multicast Telegrams twice on each bus, the function to suppress copies is mandatory also for nodes with a single bus configuration.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 6.1.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.1.1.10, PDF p.44

6.1.1.10 The format of the data added by the Safe Link Layer shall be the little endian format low-order byte first.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.2.1.1, PDF p.44

6.2.1.1 Safe Multicast message transmission implements the following:  Double transmission on each bus (time diversity)  Cyclic transmission  Sequence number  CRC according to SL  Implicit data

6.2.1.1.1 The telegrams shall have the following fixed telegram frame: Telegram header for Telegram trailer for data transmission data transmission with error detection with error detection PROFIBUS PROFIBUS Net data header trailer Sequence number CRC Command Configuration data prefix X, Y, Z Scope of this protocol description The black fields are the PROFIBUS FDL header and trailer. Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.2.1.3, PDF p.45

6.2.1.3 Sequence numbers with a value lower than or equal to a previously received one will not be forwarded to the upper layer.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.2.1.4, PDF p.45

6.2.1.4 Wrap around of the sequence number is not allowed. Wrap around of the sequence number shall be detected at the sender side. In this case the sender shall stop to send the Multicast messages.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 6.2.1.4.1, PDF p.45

6.2.1.5 Format of Implicit Data Byte Designation Range of values Meaning 1 Data_length 14..244 The length of the user data bytes (“DATA_UNIT” from the PROFIBUS FDL viewpoint) in the telegram, i.e. length of telegram header for data transmission with error detection + length of net data + length of telegram trailer for data transmission with error detection 2 Receiver_address 127 The receiver's address can be processed as implicit data because it is available on PROFIBUS FDL Level. 3 Sender_address 0..126 The sender's address can be processed as implicit data because it is available on PROFIBUS FDL Level. 4 DSAP 0..62 Destination SAP (DSAP) is equal to SSAP, see /2/. 5 SSAP 0..62 Source SAP (SSAP). Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 9.2.1.1, PDF p.50

9.3.1.1 The redundancy supervisor shall collect all telegrams received from both busses. All copies except one of a telegram shall be discarded. Only one copy of the telegram shall be sent to the Safe Link Layer.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.1.2, PDF p.50

10.1.1.1 The communication may occur between nodes of different Safety Levels.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.2, PDF p.51

10.1.1.2 For point-to-point connections the communication shall achieve a safe communication at the level of the node supporting the lowest Safety Level (see 3.3.1.4).

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.2.1, PDF p.51

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.3, PDF p.51

10.1.1.3 For multicast connections the communication shall achieve a safe communication between the sender (SIL 4, see 6.1.1.3) and receivers with different safety levels.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.4, PDF p.51

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.6, PDF p.51

10.1.1.6 For SL 2 point-to-point communication the CRC_SL2 polynomial shall be used.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.7, PDF p.51

10.1.1.7 For SL 0 point-to-point communication no CRC shall be used.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.8, PDF p.51

10.1.1.8 For multicast communication the CRC_SL4 shall be used by the sender.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.9, PDF p.51

10.1.1.9 For multicast communication the receivers shall use the CRC listed in 10.1.1.5 and

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.6, PDF p.51

10.1.1.6 according to their safety level.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.10, PDF p.51

10.1.1.10 Before calculating a CRC the initial value of all bits of the register shall be set to 0.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.11, PDF p.51

10.1.1.11 The checksum of a message shall not be used to determine the Safety Level of the message.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.12

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.12, PDF p.51

10.1.1.12 The CRC_SL2 polynomial is a factor in the CRC_SL4 polynomial. Therefore a message generated with CRC_SL4 polynomial can be checked with the CRC_SL2 polynomial. The achieved error detection capability corresponds to that of CRC_SL2.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.13

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.13, PDF p.51

10.1.1.13 This factorisation between the polynomials of different Safety Levels allows any SL 4 Multicast message to be verified by nodes supporting SL 2 and SL 4. As no CRC verification is performed by SL 0 nodes, the Multicast message can also be received by SL 0 equipments.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.1.1.13.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.1.13.1, PDF p.51

10.1.1.13.1 Note: There is a non-zero probability that the end of a message match the checksum of a higher Safety Level. This hazard has a low probability, but is mitigated by additional protection mechanism of the Safe Link Layer. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 51/62 3.1.0

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.1.3.2, PDF p.52

10.1.3.2 The generator polynomial is: CRC_SL4 = x48 + x47 + x46 + x44 + x41+ x39 + x35 + x34 + x32 + x31 + x29 + x28 + x25 + x24 + x23 + x22 + x21 + x20 + x19 + x17 + x14 + x11 + x9 + x7 + x5 + x3 + x2 + 1 = (x16 + x15 + x13 + x12 + x4 + x3 + x2 + 1) * CRC_SL2 = (x16 + x15 + x13 + x12 + x4 + x3 + x2 + 1) * (x32 + x30 + x27 + x25 + x22 + x20 + x13 + x12 + x11 + x10 + x8 + x7 + x6 + x5 + x4 + 1)

10.2 Checksum validation (non-normative)

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.1, PDF p.52

10.2.1.1 The checksums are to be validated as for normal cyclic checksums, also when validating a message generated with a higher Safety Level polynomial. At least two principles are applicable. SUBSET-057 STM FFFIS Safe Link Layer 52/62 3.1.0

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.2, PDF p.53

10.2.1.2 One method is to divide the whole message including checksum by the generator polynomial and verify that the remainder is zero.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.2.1, PDF p.53

10.2.1.2.1 Example 1: Sender: SIL 4 / Receiver: SIL 4 (based on the example in chapter 6.2.1.6) Telegram: 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h Input *): 0Eh 7Fh 53h 21h 21h 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h Polynomial: D2h 8Dh B3h FAh 4Ah ADh Result: 00h 00h 00h 00h 00h 00h *) The input for the checksum validation is the received telegram plus the implicit data.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.2.2, PDF p.53

10.2.1.2.2 Example 2: Sender: SIL 4 / Receiver: SIL 2 (based on the example in chapter 6.2.1.6) Telegram: 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h Input *): 0Eh 7Fh 53h 21h 21h 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h Polynomial: 4Ah 50h 3Dh F1h Result: 00h 00h 00h 00h *) The input for the checksum validation is the received telegram plus the implicit data.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.3, PDF p.53

10.2.1.3 The other method compares the message checksum with the computed checksum, and they shall be equal for a valid message. Remove the last bits of the message corresponding to the length of the polynomial used for verification. Divide the message (except the removed last bits) with the verification polynomial and compare with the removed bits. They shall be equal.

SUBSET-057 v3.1.0 — clause 10.2.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.3.1, PDF p.53

10.2.1.3.1 Note: In the above paragraph, the message is considered to include its checksum, so the removed part is (part of) checksum but not application data.

Citation: SUBSET-057 v3.1.0, clause 10.2.1.3.2, PDF p.53

10.2.1.3.2 Example 1: Sender: SIL 4 / Receiver: SIL 4 (based on the example in chapter 6.2.1.6) Telegram: 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h Input *): 0Eh 7Fh 53h 21h 21h 03h 00h 00h 8Dh EFh CDh ABh 89h Polynomial: D2h 8Dh B3h FAh 4Ah ADh Result: 97h E4h C3h C1h 6Ah 30h *) The input for the checksum validation is the received telegram plus the implicit data, but the last bits are removed (in this case, because of the 48 bit polynomial: 48). 9.3.7.1 If the STM uses the customisable DMI service and is configured to display such information or it uses the unified DMI service, the speed and distance supervision information sent by the STM shall be displayed by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board according to the following rules: …

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.4.1.1, PDF p.8

9.4.1.1 The size and position of NTC DMI objects shall be specified in cells using the same coordinate system with 640x480 cells as specified in 6.2. The position of an object shall be defined as the offset of the upper left corner of the object from the upper left corner of the total grid array. It shall be retrieved from the configuration data using the position identifier sent by the STM. The specification of the customisable DMI service consequently does not reuse the ETCS layout except when explicitly referring to the name of an ETCS area.

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.5.1.1.7, PDF p.9

13.5.1.1.7 ETCS speed and distance supervision a) For speed and distance supervision display in speed dial as for ETCS in area B0-B2, B6 and A2-A3 (applicable as long as the STM is active): b) Yes/No; “Yes” means that the ETCS train speed display is re- used as such together with the supervision information as specified in 13.4.6. “No” means that there is no display of speed and distance supervision in the ETCS way. c) if Yes: speed dial range (0-140/180/250/400 km/h or same range as ETCS).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.5.1.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.5.1.1.10, PDF p.9

13.5.1.1.10 Moved areas of the ETCS layout: a) If a STM needs partially or totally the cells used by an area defined in the ETCS layout and in which ETCS DMI objects are displayed in level NTC modes SN or NL, the ETCS objects displayed in it must be moved somewhere else on the national layout. Therefore it shall be possible to specify a changed location for moving the following ETCS areas and their related ETCS objects. For buttons also the new related soft key (F1-F5) must be defined:  Areas F1-F5 for the buttons for selecting the main, override, data view, special or settings window;  Area A4 for the adhesion “slippery rail”;  Areas B7 and C8 for the ETCS mode and level display; Version 3.1.0  Area C1 for the mode/level acknowledgements;  Area C7 for the Override status indication;  Area C9 for the brake indication;  Area E1 for safe radio connection indication;  Area G13 for local time b) The new location shall be specified by a new x:y position in cells. c) The moved areas shall have the same size as the original ETCS areas.

1.2.2 Relevant requirements

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 1.2.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 1.2.2.1, PDF p.16

1.2.2.1 ETCS DMI Specification [12] Chapter Text Version 3.1.0

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.1.2, PDF p.17

9.3.1.2 The colours requested by the text, indicator or button attribute of a STM request shall be displayed with RGB values as specified for ETCS objects in Table 4. The additional colours not specified for ETCS objects shall be displayed with the RGB values in Table 19.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.1, PDF p.17

9.3.2.1 When flashing style ‘yellow frame’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall be surrounded by a flashing frame as specified in 5.1.1.3.1.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.2, PDF p.17

9.3.2.2 When flashing style ‘whole area’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall toggle between visible and not visible state (i.e. the dark blue background colour).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.3, PDF p.17

9.3.2.3 Flashing of different objects shall be synchronised: all objects with normal flashing mode and the same frequency shall be in the same state at the same time; objects with counterphase flashing shall be in the alternative state at this time.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.1, PDF p.17

9.3.4.1 An NTC indicator can display text and/or an icon. Its state may change by changing the contained text, icon, text colour, text background colour or flashing mode. Additionally its position may change.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.1, PDF p.17

9.3.4.2.1 The caption text shall always be visible when no icon is requested by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.2, PDF p.17

9.3.4.2.2 If the STM uses the customisable DMI, the caption text shall also be visible, if “display of text upon icon” is requested as corresponding icon attribute in the configuration data.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.3, PDF p.17

9.3.4.2.3 Otherwise the caption text shall be ignored by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.3, PDF p.17

9.3.4.3 An indicator shall be displayed according to the display attribute sent with the indicator Request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.4, PDF p.17

9.3.4.4 If both the caption text and the icon are displayed, the layering shall be text in foreground, icon in middle layer and background colour in background.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.5, PDF p.17

9.3.4.5 The part of the caption text from the seventh character shall be displayed on a second Line.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.4.1.3, PDF p.17

9.4.1.3 The customisable DMI service shall display icons centred in the specified area.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 1.2.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 1.2.2.2, PDF p.17

1.2.2.2 For ERTMS/ETCS on-board from FFFIS STM specification [3] Chapter Text

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.1, PDF p.17

13.4.1.1 The DMI objects indicators and buttons used by the different STMs are assigned a unique object identity made of NID_STM and Indicator/Button Identifier.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.2, PDF p.17

13.4.1.2 The STM Identity is implicitly provided by the STM by its announced NID_STM (and repeated in each message header according to the language).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.3, PDF p.17

13.4.1.3 The Indicator/Button Identifier is provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.4, PDF p.17

13.4.1.4 The Indicator/Button Identifier is used by the STM to be able to change the state of objects and to move or remove them. The Button Identifier is also used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to transmit the button events to the STM. If the customisable DMI service is used, it is also used to define the properties of the object.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.5, PDF p.17

13.4.1.5 All icons (bitmap symbols) used by the different STMs using a customisable DMI are assigned an icon identity made of NID_STM and Icon Identifier.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.6, PDF p.17

13.4.1.6 An Icon Identifier can be provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.9, PDF p.17

13.4.1.9 For specifying the position of DMI objects, Position Identifiers are used.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.10, PDF p.17

13.4.1.10 If the unified DMI service is used, the Position Identifier specifies an area of Version 3.1.0 the ETCS layout as defined in [12].

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.11, PDF p.18

13.4.1.11 If the customisable DMI service is used, the Position Identifier and the NID_STM are used to define the position in cell coordinates and size as specified in the configuration data for this STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.3, PDF p.18

13.4.3.3 The Icon Identifier shall be used by the DMI Function in case of the customisable DMI service to retrieve from the configuration data the corresponding icon attached to an Indicator/Button object.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.4, PDF p.18

13.4.3.4 The display attribute shall specify the background colour and the flashing mode for the whole Indicator and the display colour of the caption text.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.5, PDF p.18

13.4.3.5 The flashing mode specifies if the slow, fast or no flashing and if normal or counterphase flashing shall be used

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 15.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 15.1.1.1, PDF p.18

15.1.1.1 The maximum number of characters (coded in UTF-8 by 1 or 2 bytes) to display shall be b) 12 characters for button and indicator caption text in button and indicator requests.

13.4.3.2 The STM shall request the display of an Indicator by means of the following definition: a) its Indicator Identifier, b) an optional Icon Identifier, c) an optional caption text, d) a Position Identifier, e) a display attribute.

1.3.2.1 ETCS DMI Specification [12] Chapter Text

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.1.2, PDF p.27

9.3.1.2 The colours requested by the text, indicator or button attribute of a STM request shall be displayed with RGB values as specified for ETCS objects in Table 4. The additional colours not specified for ETCS objects shall be displayed with the RGB values in Table 19.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.1, PDF p.27

9.3.2.1 When flashing style ‘yellow frame’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall be surrounded by a flashing frame as specified in 5.1.1.3.1.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.2, PDF p.27

9.3.2.2 When flashing style ‘whole area’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall toggle between visible and not visible state (i.e. the dark blue background colour).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.2.3, PDF p.27

9.3.2.3 Flashing of different objects shall be synchronised: all objects with normal flashing mode and the same frequency shall be in the same state at the same time; objects with counterphase flashing shall be in the alternative state at this time.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.1, PDF p.27

9.3.4.1 An NTC indicator can display text and/or an icon. Its state may change by changing the contained text, icon, text colour, text background colour or flashing mode. Additionally its position may change.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.1, PDF p.27

9.3.4.2.1 The caption text shall always be visible when no icon is requested by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.2, PDF p.27

9.3.4.2.2 If the STM uses the customisable DMI, the caption text shall also be visible, if “display of text upon icon” is requested as corresponding icon attribute in the configuration data.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.2.3, PDF p.27

9.3.4.2.3 Otherwise the caption text shall be ignored by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.3, PDF p.27

9.3.4.3 An indicator shall be displayed according to the display attribute sent with the indicator Request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.4, PDF p.27

9.3.4.4 If both the caption text and the icon are displayed, the layering shall be text in foreground, icon in middle layer and background colour in background.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.4.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.4.5, PDF p.27

9.3.4.5 The part of the caption text from the seventh character shall be displayed on a second Line.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.5.1, PDF p.27

9.3.5.1 Buttons are a pure functional extension of Indicators. All requirements of chapter 9.3.4 shall apply to buttons, by replacing “indicator” with “button”.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.5.2, PDF p.27

9.3.5.2 The ERTMS/ETCS-onboard shall display NTC buttons pressed and not pressed like ETCS buttons.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.4.1.3, PDF p.27

9.4.1.3 The customisable DMI service shall display icons centred in the specified area.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 1.3.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 1.3.2.2, PDF p.27

1.3.2.2 For ERTMS/ETCS on-board from FFFIS STM specification [3] Chapter Text

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.1, PDF p.27

13.4.1.1 The DMI objects indicators and buttons used by the different STMs are assigned a unique object identity made of NID_STM and Indicator/Button Identifier.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.2, PDF p.27

13.4.1.2 The STM Identity is implicitly provided by the STM by its announced NID_STM (and repeated in each message header according to the language).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.3, PDF p.27

13.4.1.3 The Indicator/Button Identifier is provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.4, PDF p.27

13.4.1.4 The Indicator/Button Identifier is used by the STM to be able to change the state of objects and to move or remove them. The Button Identifier is also Version 3.1.0 used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to transmit the button events to the STM. If the customisable DMI service is used, it is also used to define the properties of the object.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.5, PDF p.28

13.4.1.5 All icons (bitmap symbols) used by the different STMs using a customisable DMI are assigned an icon identity made of NID_STM and Icon Identifier.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.6, PDF p.28

13.4.1.6 An Icon Identifier can be provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.9, PDF p.28

13.4.1.9 For specifying the position of DMI objects, Position Identifiers are used.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.10, PDF p.28

13.4.1.10 If the unified DMI service is used, the Position Identifier specifies an area of the ETCS layout as defined in [12].

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.1.11, PDF p.28

13.4.1.11 If the customisable DMI service is used, the Position Identifier and the NID_STM are used to define the position in cell coordinates and size as specified in the configuration data for this STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.3, PDF p.28

13.4.3.3 The Icon Identifier shall be used by the DMI Function in case of the customisable DMI service to retrieve from the configuration data the corresponding icon attached to an Indicator/Button object.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.4, PDF p.28

13.4.3.4 The display attribute shall specify the background colour and the flashing mode for the whole Indicator and the display colour of the caption text.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.5, PDF p.28

13.4.3.5 The flashing mode specifies if the slow, fast or no flashing and if normal or counterphase flashing shall be used

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 15.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 15.1.1.1, PDF p.28

15.1.1.1 The maximum number of characters (coded in UTF-8 by 1 or 2 bytes) to display shall be b) 12 characters for button and indicator caption text in button and indicator requests.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.4.1, PDF p.28

13.4.4.1 Buttons are a pure functional extension of Indicators. All requirements of chapter 13.4.3 shall apply to Buttons, by replacing “Indicator” with “Button”

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.4.2, PDF p.28

13.4.4.2 The extension is the transmission of Button events from the DMI Function to STM. The DMI Function shall make a distinction between push event (transition from Button not pressed to pressed state) and release event (opposite transition).

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.4.3, PDF p.28

13.4.4.3 The DMI Function shall report Button push and release events to the STM and shall timestamp those event reports to reflect the sequence of events.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.4.4, PDF p.28

13.4.4.4 The DMI Function shall use the Reference Time (see chapter 5.2.2) for timestamping the Button events reports.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.1, PDF p.32

13.4.2.1 The DMI Function shall display a text message when requested by the STM. The text message request shall consist of a Text Identifier, a string of text to be shown to the driver, a display attribute and a possible request for driver acknowledgement.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.2, PDF p.32

13.4.2.2 The DMI Function shall report to the STM the acknowledgement of text messages (which were required to be acknowledged) from the driver referencing the corresponding Text Identifier.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.3, PDF p.32

13.4.2.3 The DMI Function shall delete a text message when requested by the active STM. The request shall reference the Text Identifier of the text message to be deleted.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.4, PDF p.32

13.4.2.4 If the STM requests a text message with the same Text Identifier as a not yet deleted text message, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete the original text message and display the new requested text message

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.5, PDF p.32

13.4.2.5 The display attribute specifies the colour of the text, its background colour, the flashing mode and the group of text messages.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.6, PDF p.32

13.4.2.6 The flashing mode specifies if the slow, fast or no flashing and if normal or counterphase flashing shall be used.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1, PDF p.40

9.3.7.1 If the STM uses the customisable DMI service and is configured to display such information or it uses the unified DMI service, the speed and distance supervision information sent by the STM shall be displayed by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board according to the following rules:

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.1, PDF p.40

9.3.7.1.1 The current train speed pointer shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.1.2 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.2, PDF p.40

9.3.7.1.2 The current train speed digital shall be displayed as specified in 8.3.1.3.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.3, PDF p.40

9.3.7.1.3 When requested by the display mode sent by the STM, the distance to target bar shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.2.1. Version 3.1.0

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.4, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.4 When requested by the display mode sent by the STM, the distance to target digital shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.2.2.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.5, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.5 When the supervision speeds are requested to be displayed as bars, the width of those speed bars shall be 9 cells, except for: a) the part of the permitted speed bar below a release speed bar, b) the release speed bar, c) the intervention speed bar if it is requested to display it with the “wide bar width”.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.6, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.6 When a release speed bar is displayed, the permitted speed bar and the release speed bar shall be indicated applying clause 8.2.1.6.4 by analogy to the CSG.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.7, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.7 When the intervention speed bar is requested to be displayed with “wide bar width”, it shall be displayed with 20 cells.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 The speed bars and hooks shall be displayed along the speed dial in the area B2 as for the Circular speed gauge and for the Basic speed hook(s) used on the ETCS default window, except consideration of the display mode.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 a) a) A dark grey bar below 0km/h (-149 degrees to -144 degrees, as specified for ETCS default window) if display of any bar is requested.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 b) b) The target speed bar in the colour requested for target speed between permitted speed and target speed if permitted speed is displayed and is lower than target speed, otherwise between 0km/h and target speed.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 c) c) If the requested display mode is ‘hook only’, the target speed hook shall be displayed at the target speed as specified in 8.2.1.5.5 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 d) d) If the requested display mode is ‘hook and bar’, the target speed hook shall be displayed at the target speed as specified in 8.2.1.4.7 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 e) e) The permitted speed bar in the colour requested for permitted speed between target speed and permitted speed if target speed is displayed and is lower than permitted speed, otherwise between 0km/h and permitted speed, if no target speed is displayed. The permitted speed bar may overlap with the release speed bar.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 f) f) If the requested display mode is ‘hook only’, the permitted speed hook shall be displayed at the permitted speed as specified in 8.2.1.5.4 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 g) g) If the requested display mode is ‘hook and bar’, the permitted speed hook shall be displayed at the permitted speed as specified in 8.2.1.4.7 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 h) h) The intervention speed bar between permitted speed and intervention speed in the colour requested for intervention speed.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 i) i) The release speed bar between 0km/h and release speed, possibly overlapping with permitted speed bar in the colour requested for the release speed.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.8 j) j) The order of superimposing objects on top of the background from back to front is: intervention speed bar, target speed bar/hook, permitted speed bar/hook, release speed bar.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.3.7.1.9, PDF p.41

9.3.7.1.9 The release speed digital display shall be displayed in the colour requested for the release speed.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.5.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.5.2.4, PDF p.41

9.5.2.4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall display the NTC supervision information using the same range for the speed dial as for ETCS supervision information Version 3.1.0

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 3.5.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 3.5.7.1, PDF p.52

3.5.7.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall inform the driver about the status of the safe radio connection. To that purpose, the following indication statuses of the safe radio connection are defined: “No Connection”, “Connection Lost/Set-Up failed”, “Connection Up”.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 5.10.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 5.10.4.1, PDF p.52

5.10.4.1 If defined so for the level transition (see table below), the driver shall be requested to acknowledge the transition a) when the max safe front end of the train has passed a trackside defined location in rear of the level transition border b) upon receipt of the order to switch to the new level immediately.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 5.10.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 5.10.4.2, PDF p.52

5.10.4.2 If the driver has not yet acknowledged within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A3.1) after the level transition, a service brake command shall be initiated.

9.2.1.1 The ETCS objects/functions in document [3] chapter 4.7.2, modes SN and NL shall be displayed as far as they concern a default window, i.e. the appearance shall be as specified in chapter 8 but the location of the ETCS objects/functions will be according to the definition of the NTC default window of the corresponding National System.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.2.1.2, PDF p.53

9.2.1.2 The ETCS buttons accessing the sub-level windows shall be available with the labels as specified in 8.5 but with their size and location depending on the ergonomic arrangements of areas of the NTC default window of the corresponding National System.

13.5.1.1 The configuration of the customisable DMI shall define the following data for each STM using the customisable DMI service:

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.5.1.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.5.1.1.10, PDF p.53

13.5.1.1.10 Moved areas of the ETCS layout: a) If a STM needs partially or totally the cells used by an area defined in the ETCS layout and in which ETCS DMI objects are displayed in level NTC modes SN or NL, the ETCS objects displayed in it must be moved somewhere else on the national layout. Therefore it shall be possible to specify a changed location for moving the following ETCS areas and their related ETCS objects. For buttons also the new related soft key (F1-F5) must be defined:  Areas F1-F5 for the buttons for selecting the main, override, data view, special or settings window;  Area A4 for the adhesion “slippery rail”;  Areas B7 and C8 for the ETCS mode and level display;  Area C1 for the mode/level acknowledgements;  Area C7 for the Override status indication;  Area C9 for the brake indication;  Area E1 for safe radio connection indication;  Area G13 for local time b) The new location shall be specified by a new x:y position in cells. c) The moved areas shall have the same size as the original ETCS areas. Version 3.1.0

5.3.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall allow the STM to access its functions and resources according to the following table: a) x = access is allowed in all Levels b) (x) = access is allowed in all Levels if possible c) s = access is only allowed for an active STM (see chapter 4.1.1.3) d) h = access is allowed for an STM in HS for preliminary request for DMI objects (see 13.2.1.5) ERTMS/ETCS N S P S F L S OS S N U T P S I S R ON-BOARD P B S H S S R L L N R T F S N V functions and resources available for STMs DMI Function h h h h h s, h h h s, h h

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.1, PDF p.55

13.2.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall only allow the active STM to communicate with the driver.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.2, PDF p.55

13.2.1.2 When the STM is no more active (see 4.1.1.3), the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all DMI objects controlled by this STM.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.3, PDF p.55

13.2.1.3 When the connection between an STM and the DMI Function is disconnected, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all the DMI objects controlled by this STM (including preliminary requests) after a timeout of 2 seconds.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.4, PDF p.55

13.2.1.4 When the connection between the active STM and the DMI Function is lost and reestablished within the timeout of 2 seconds, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all the DMI objects controlled by the STM when the DMI connection to the STM is established.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.5, PDF p.55

13.2.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall be able to receive and store preliminary request for DMI objects from an STM being in HS state and display them immediately after having received the DA state report.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.2.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.2.1.6, PDF p.55

13.2.1.6 When an STM reports PO, CS or FA, or is considered as failed, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard shall delete all preliminary requests for DMI objects from this STM.

5.4.3.2 Start of Mission Procedure, step S0: The Start of Mission procedure shall be engaged when the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment is in Stand-By mode with a desk open and no communication session is established or is being established.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 5.4.3.2

5.4.3.2 Start of Mission Procedure, step S10: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall offer the possibility to the driver to select SH, NL, or to select Train Data Entry. ... ...  If the driver selects Train Data Entry (E11), the process shall go to S12 ..

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 5.4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 5.4.3.2, PDF p.59

5.4.3.2 Start of Mission Procedure, step S20: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall offer the possibility to the driver to select “Start” a) When the validated level is NTC and the driver selects "start" (E20), the process shall go to S22...

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 5.4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 5.4.3.2, PDF p.59

5.4.3.2 Start of Mission Procedure, step S22: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request an acknowledgement from the driver for running under supervision of the selected National System. When the driver acknowledges (E30), the mission starts in SN mode (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes). Following E30, if the position is still invalid, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete the train position data (new status: “unknown”). 5.10.3.15.1 In addition to the level transitions ordered by trackside, it is also possible, at standstill, for the driver to change the ERTMS/ETCS level (refer to section 3.18.4.2).

2.10 General remarks for Test Cases of FID 7 The time between test steps in the following test specifications is generally chosen thus that the expected output reactions are performed by the DUT before the next test step is triggered. If the check of DMI outputs is performed manually it may however be necessary to increase the time between the steps, in order to give the tester time to verify the expected test results. In this FID there are no STM test cases, because it is optional for the STMs to use the DMI function of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board. For the following test case specifications also a short message format is used besides the full message format as specified in chapter 1 of SUBSET-074. The full message format has one line for each message variable, specifying the variable name, length in bits, value and description. The short message format has one line for simple packets and one line per 1-3 iterated sub structures for packets with iterations. The short message format specifies a packet by its packet number and the sequence of variables. A variable is specified by its shortened variable name and value plus an optional description. The short message format is only used, if a similar packet with the same identifier has been presented for the same test case before. Version 3.1.0 2 samples are presented below. Version 3.1.0

ERTMS/ETCS requirements Subset-035: 10.10.2.1, 10.10.2.2, 10.10.2.3 a) tested Subset-026: 5.8.3.7.1 STM requirements tested Subset-035: Subset-026: Packets transmitted via Packet STM-6, STM-7, STM-15 FFFIS STM ERTMS/ETCS on-board - To perform this test case it is necessary to connect at least 2 STMs to the ETCS on-board. configuration Comments and constraints The objective of this test is to check  that the ERTMS/ETCS on-board (STM Control Function) while in Level NTC reports the ETCS Override Status to all connected STMs, after the STM in the state DA has reported the activation of its override function according to the national requirements to the ETCS on-board (STM Control Function), and  that the ERTMS/ETCS on-board (STM Control Function) reports the deactivation of the ETCS Override Status to all connected STMs whenever the ETCS Override Status is deactivated according to the ERTMS/ETCS rules.  that the ERTMS/ETCS on-board resets the override procedure when new activation report from STM is received  that the (ETCS) override symbol is not shown for an override procedure activated by a STM. SUBSET-038 v3.1.0 — clause 3.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-038 v3.1.0, clause 3.1.1.1, PDF p.6

3.1.1.1 No operational intervention is normally necessary to allow a duly authorised OBU to traverse into several separately controlled ERTMS areas, provided that the relevant preparatory actions have been carried out in advance of arrival at each area. Among these actions specific KM functions are also required to establish interoperable services.

SUBSET-038 v3.1.0 — clause 3.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-038 v3.1.0, clause 3.1.1.2, PDF p.6

3.1.1.2 For KMC interworking, a FIS (Functional Interface Specification) is required at the KMC-KMC interface. This is the purpose of this document, which describes the principles and procedures including the use of additional K-KMC keys required to exchange KMACs and allow interoperable train traffic between KM domains. It also describes general concepts, principles, functions and procedures to manage cryptographic materials used by the EuroRadio safety layer for ERTMS/ETCS applications.

SUBSET-038 v3.1.0 — clause 3.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-038 v3.1.0, clause 3.1.1.3, PDF p.6

3.1.1.3 This specification covers management of Symmetric Key Material using symmetric procedures.

3.2.1.1 This document is related to the key management of the following ERTMS entities: - OBU - RIU - RBC - KMC

3.2.1.3 The document covers Off-line exchange needed between KM domains to manage different sets of ERTMS entities and allow railway traffic running in a fully controlled and interoperable way.
